idiom_name: facade class over cppzmq (zmq::socket_t send/recv) or AMQP-CPP
implementation_notes: The classic gateway class is expressible in C++ but nothing generates it: declare a small interface (InventoryGateway with checkStock(sku)) and implement it in a class that owns a cppzmq zmq::socket_t or an AMQP-CPP channel - typed arguments go in, a typed value comes back, and only the implementation sees the wire. The blocking REQ/REP form (send, then recv on the same socket) is the default because it matches the method-call illusion; with C++20 the same facade can expose co_await-able completions instead of blocking. Keep the interface-plus-implementation split even when caller and callee share a team: that seam is what lets tests substitute a fake broker and what keeps the messaging headers out of business code.
pitfalls: A cppzmq socket is not thread-safe and REQ/REP additionally demands strict send-then-recv alternation, so one gateway instance must be confined to one thread or guarded.
The zmq::context_t must outlive every socket it created: destroying it while the gateway still holds sockets makes the next send fail (ETERM).
cppzmq reports failures through return values and error codes rather than exceptions, so the gateway has to invent the failure contract (and decide what a timeout means).
Copying the socket or the facade instead of sharing a reference silently creates a second REQ socket and breaks the lockstep state.
